wu: Warm-up: 'Food Category Race' — Students stand in two teams. Teacher calls out a food group (e.g., 'fruits'), one student from each team runs to the board to write one correct word. First to write a valid word gets a point. Repeat with 'vegetables', 'dairy', etc.
wuAlt: Alternative 1: 'I went to the market' — Students sit in a circle. First student says 'I went to the market and bought an apple.' Next student repeats and adds another item (e.g., 'I went to the market and bought an apple and some milk.').
Alternative 2: 'Flashcard Quick Sort' — Teacher shows food flashcards; students shout 'countable!' or 'uncountable!' as quickly as possible.
pres: Presentation: Show a simple Thanksgiving recipe (e.g., cranberry sauce) on the board. Highlight quantifiers: 'a cup of sugar', 'a few cranberries', 'too much water'. Elicit countable/uncountable nouns and model sentences like 'How much sugar?' 'How many cranberries?' Check understanding with quick thumbs-up/down for true/false statements about the recipe.
presAlt: Alternative 1: Use realia (empty cups, spoons) to demonstrate quantities. Students say 'How much?' or 'How many?' as you pour/show items.
Alternative 2: Show a short video clip of a cooking show with clear quantifiers; students note down examples they hear.
prac: Guided practice: 'Recipe Fill-in' — Students work in pairs to complete a worksheet with a recipe using 'a little', 'a few', 'some', 'any', 'too much/many'. Teacher monitors and corrects errors. Then, pairs swap worksheets and check answers together.
pracAlt: Alternative 1: 'Quantifier Bingo' — Teacher calls out sentences like 'I have too many potatoes'; students cross off matching pictures on their bingo cards.
Alternative 2: 'Find Someone Who...' — Students walk around asking 'Do you have any apples at home?' and 'Do you eat too much sugar?' to find classmates who say yes.
ls: Listening slot: Students listen to a recording of a Thanksgiving recipe (e.g., pumpkin pie) and fill in missing quantities on a worksheet. They then compare answers in pairs before a class check. This checks their ability to catch specific quantifiers in context.
re: Reactivation game: 'Stand Up If...' — Teacher says prompts like 'Stand up if you like a little honey in your tea' or 'Stand up if you eat too many oranges'. Students stand up or sit down based on their preferences, moving their bodies to re-engage.
prod: Production task: 'Two-Corners Debate' — Label corners 'Traditional Thanksgiving' and 'Moroccan Harvest Feast'. Students choose a corner and discuss in groups: 'Which foods are better? Why?' After 5 minutes, they switch corners and argue the opposite side. Encourage using 'a little', 'a few', 'too much/many' in their arguments.
rw: Reading and writing slot: Students read a short text comparing Thanksgiving and Moroccan harvest customs (e.g., Aid al-Fitr or Green March). They then write 3-4 sentences about one custom they find interesting, using quantifiers like 'many people' or 'a little food'.
st: Story/Song + Goodbye: Play a short animated story about gratitude (e.g., 'The Thankful Turkey'). End with the goodbye routine: 'Today we learned to describe recipes with quantities. Thank you, class! Have a great day!'
g: Students race to write food words on the board in teams.
Pairs complete a recipe worksheet with correct quantifiers.
Students cross off pictures matching teacher's sentences.
Students stand/sit based on food preference prompts.
Students debate food traditions, switching sides mid-activity.
diff: Fast finishers: Write a 60-word email describing their favorite recipe using 5+ quantifiers.
Support: Use a word bank with quantifiers and countable/uncountable nouns during the debate.
hw: Homework 1: Read a short text about Thanksgiving foods; answer 3 questions in full sentences using 'how much/many'.
Homework 2: Interview 3 people: 'What are you thankful for?'; report back in 2-3 sentences each.
Homework 3: Write a simple recipe for a Moroccan dish using 'a little', 'a few', 'some', 'any'.
tip: Tip: Use local harvest festivals (like Green March) to bridge cultural gaps and make quantifiers more relevant. Compare quantities in Moroccan dishes (e.g., 'a little cumin', 'many onions') to reinforce learning.
